record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Is there a pure morphic binary word avoiding 2-abelian cubes?

evidence.quote: Is there a pure morphic binary word avoiding 2-abelian cubes?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma=\{0,1\}$ be the binary alphabet, and let $\Sigma^*$ (resp. $\Sigma^\omega$) denote the set of finite (resp. one-sided infinite) words over $\Sigma$. For a word $w\in\Sigma^*$ and a positive integer $k$, let $|w|_u$ denote the number of occurrences of the factor $u\in\Sigma^*$ in $w$. Two finite words $u,v$ are said to be $k$-abelian equivalent, written $u\sim_k v$, if $|u|_x=|v|_x$ for every $x\in\Sigma^*$ with $|x|\le k$. (Equivalently, $u\sim_k v$ iff $u$ and $v$ have the same prefix and suffix of length $k-1$ and the same multiset of factors of length $k$.) A $2$-abelian cube is a nonempty word of the form $w_1w_2w_3$ with $w_1\sim_2 w_2\sim_2 w_3$. An infinite word $\mathbf{w}\in\Sigma^\omega$ avoids $2$-abelian cubes if no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is a $2$-abelian cube.

A morphism is a map $h:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ satisfying $h(xy)=h(x)h(y)$. An infinite word $\mathbf{w}\in\Sigma^\omega$ is called pure morphic if there exist a morphism $h:\Sigma^*\to\Sigma^*$ and a letter $a\in\Sigma$ with $h(a)=ax$ for some nonempty $x\in\Sigma^*$ such that $\mathbf{w}=\lim_{n\to\infty} h^n(a)$, the fixed point of $h$ starting with $a$.

Question: Does there exist a pure morphic infinite word $\mathbf{w}\in\Sigma^\omega$ that avoids $2$-abelian cubes?
artifact.status_search_result: It is known that 2-abelian cubes are avoidable on a binary alphabet (proved via constructions including morphic images), and that 3-abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets. However, whether such an infinite binary word avoiding 2-abelian cubes can be obtained as a pure morphic word (a fixed point of a single iterated morphism, not merely a morphic image) does not appear to have been resolved in the literature; results on related k-abelian square-freeness suggest pure morphic constructions are often insufficient. Status appears to remain open/unknown.

status_evidence.title: 3-Abelian Cubes Are Avoidable on Binary Alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Proves k-abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets for k>=3.
status_evidence.claim: 2-abelian cube avoidance on binary remains the boundary case; 3-abelian cube avoidance is established.

status_evidence.title: 5-abelian cubes are avoidable on binary alphabets
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier result establishing avoidability for k>=5.
status_evidence.claim: Progress on k-abelian cube avoidance on binary alphabets.

status_evidence.title: Rosenfeld PhD thesis
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses k-abelian power avoidance and limitations of pure morphic constructions.
status_evidence.claim: Pure morphic constructions are often insufficient for k-abelian avoidance problems.
